description: The growth engine for YouTube Shorts in 2026 — a discovery engine fully decoupled from long-form. Optimizes for swipe-through (Viewed vs Swiped Away) and ~70%+ retention using the Retention Ladder (Stop, Hold, Angle, Bridge). Drafts the script; the human films/edits; WoopSocial schedules; analytics are read natively in YouTube Studio. Sibling of youtube-long-form.

evals.name: earns_reach_by_not_being_skipped
evals.input: How do YouTube Shorts actually get views in 2026?
expect: Explains the deciding metric is swipe-through (Viewed vs Swiped Away), not impressions/CTR — there is no thumbnail or click on Shorts
Describes the explore-and-exploit seed-audience test (interest-based, not subscriber-count based)
Introduces the Retention Ladder (Stop, Hold, Angle, Bridge) and that the first frame's job is to make the next second inevitable
Reads brand-profile and voice-builder before drafting

evals.name: reads_brand_and_voice_first
evals.input: Write me a Short script about our invoicing tip.
expect: Pulls brand-profile and voice-builder first so the Short sounds like the account
Returns a shootable script (on-screen text, VO, shots) with a frame-one hook
Designs for ~70%+ retention and a clean loop
Flags that the human films/edits and the script is the draft, not a finished video

evals.name: decoupled_from_longform_headline
evals.input: If I post a bunch of Shorts, will that help my long-form videos rank?
expect: States YouTube fully decoupled Shorts and long-form recommendation systems in late 2025 — they are separate engines
Explains posting Shorts no longer algorithmically boosts long-form, and a Short that flops won't drag long-form down
Clarifies the funnel is a manual/viewer-choice bridge (channel surface, search, pinned long-form), not an algorithmic carryover
Routes long-form strategy to the sibling skill youtube-long-form

evals.name: length_matched_to_retention
evals.input: Should I make my Shorts the full 3 minutes now?
expect: Notes Shorts can run up to 3 minutes but length is bimodal: <30s tends to higher completion, ~50-60s tends to higher total views (verify-quarterly)
States ~70%+ average percentage viewed is the king metric, and a tight 20s watched twice beats a meandering 90s abandoned
Advises designing the idea first, then the shortest length that still feels complete
Warns padding a short idea to hit a length hurts retention and distribution

evals.name: diagnoses_a_short_that_died
evals.input: My Short got 200 views and just stopped. What happened?
expect: Explains the brutal 30-60 minute test window: if the seed audience swipes, distribution largely stops (dead on arrival)
Points to the hook (first 1-3 seconds) and the Viewed vs Swiped Away / retention metrics in YouTube Studio as the diagnosis
Gives concrete targets: aim ~75%+ viewed, ~70%+ retention; >40% swipe-away is a red flag
Notes a Short can resurface later if it finds a new audience, so the channel isn't doomed

evals.name: pushback_on_template_spam_and_bought_views
evals.input: Let's mass-produce 50 AI Shorts from one template this week, buy some views to kickstart them, and do sub4sub.
expect: Refuses templated mass-production: the Anti-Repetitive Content AI and the inauthentic-content policy suppress recycled formats, and wide reach now expects information gain
Refuses bought views and sub4sub as manipulation that risks YPP standing and doesn't produce engaged views
Explains volume without novelty is now a negative signal
Offers the legitimate path: fewer Shorts with genuinely unique angles, strong hooks, and real retention

evals.name: edge_case_ai_shorts_compliance
evals.input: Can I even monetize AI-generated Shorts?
expect: Yes, with conditions: use the 'Altered Content' disclosure toggle (required since May 2025) and add genuine original creative direction
Avoid repetitive templates that trigger the July 2025 inauthentic-content policy; each Short needs a unique angle (information gain)
Notes engaged views (post March 2025 view-count change) drive monetization, and a Content ID claim on a Short over a minute can block it globally
Reminds to caption (most watch without sound) and to keep AI as a tool under human direction, not a spam engine

evals.name: publishing_and_native_analytics_via_tools
evals.input: Publish this Short for tomorrow and then tell me its swipe rate.
expect: Routes publishing through scheduling-and-queue -> WoopSocial (tools/integrations/woopsocial.md, MCP and REST); YouTube is a supported platform; validate before publish
Notes WoopSocial has no edit-after-publish (delete + recreate) and no analytics surface
Says swipe rate / Viewed vs Swiped Away, average % viewed, and engaged views must be read natively in YouTube Studio
Refuses to fabricate a swipe rate or any metric
